# Category catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/export-skill-catalog.ts in the Foundation app repo. Don't edit by hand. -->

When connected, `describe_categories` returns the same information live and takes precedence over this file.

Columns marked *computed* are derived by the engine: you can leave them out. "currency" means the project's currency.

Always on (never listed in the active category arrays): capex `pre-operational`, opex `human-resources`, revenue `revenue`.

## Operating (opex) categories

### `raw-materials`: Raw Materials & Components (default 0% fixed)

Monthly consumption of every raw material or purchased part in the bill of materials. For a restaurant or coffee shop, define recipes on the Ingredients & Recipes step instead. Quantities here fill in automatically from planned sales volume.

| `material` | Material | text |  |
| `notes` | Notes | text |  |
| `specs` | Technical specs | text |  |

| `qty` | Annual qty | *computed* |  |
| `unit` | Unit | text |  |
| `unitCost` | Unit cost | number | currency |
| `total` | Total cost | *computed* | currency |

### `human-resources`: Human Resources (default 100% fixed)

Headcount and pay by role, from management to production and support staff. Monthly salary is gross, per person. The actual cost of employing someone is usually higher once payroll tax, mandatory social-security/insurance contributions, and benefits are added on top, so there's a separate field for that.

| key | label | type | unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `role` | Role | text |  |
| `notes` | Notes | text |  |
| `headcount` | Headcount | number |  |
| `monthlySalary` | Monthly salary / person (gross) | number | currency |
| `employerBurdenPct` | Employer burden on top of gross | number | % |
| `annualCost` | Annual cost | *computed* | currency |

## Revenue categories

### `revenue`: Products & Revenue

Three kinds of product live here: priced per unit (a coffee, a one-off sale), priced as a commission (a % of a contract/transaction value that flows through you), or a subscription with its own customer count and an optional one-time fee that only fires when a customer is new. The wizard shows them as separate tables so each only shows the columns it needs; all of them add up into one total revenue. Growth is one rate for everything (Financial Assumptions); subscriptions also share one churn rate there. "Starts after" is a delay in months, not years. A product that needs 6 months of build time before it can sell anything ramps in at half a year's revenue in year 1, not zero.

| key | label | type | unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `product` | Product | text |  |
| `notes` | Notes | text |  |
| `unitPrice` | Unit price | number | currency |
| `monthlyVolume` | Monthly volume | number |  |
| `annualVolume` | Annual volume | *computed* |  |
| `basisAmount` | Monthly contract value | number | currency |
| `basisPct` | Commission rate | number | % |
| `startCustomers` | At start | number |  |
| `endCustomersYear1` | By end of Year 1 | number |  |
| `monthlyRecurringPrice` | Monthly price | number | currency |
| `onboardingPrice` | One-time fee | number | currency |
| `startMonth` | Starts after | number | months |
| `totalSales` | Total sales | *computed* | currency |

## Revenue `pricingMode`

Every revenue row carries `pricingMode`: `unit` (unitPrice × monthlyVolume), `commission` (basisAmount × basisPct%), or `subscription` (startCustomers → endCustomersYear1 at monthlyRecurringPrice, plus onboardingPrice per new customer). Fill only the fields its mode uses; leave the others 0.
